Novel Craft 1.1 turns every note into a page you read and edit like a document, links each note's family beside it, and adds chapter renumbering, an archive, and shared power levels. Everything since 1.0.0 is listed below.

## Note pages

- Notes are documents: the page in the middle, long text as sections, and a column beside it with what the note relates to. The same page shows in the drawer and in left-drawer tabs.
- Data store and taxonomy notes group their fields under **Details**, **Description** and **Info**. Novels, unit and recipe moved to **Links & more**; yes/no fields are switches.
- Descriptions and other long text fields use the block editor and show formatted. Pasted paragraphs keep their formatting.
- **Save** and **Discard** sit under the section being edited. Ctrl+S closes a section with no changes, and Escape twice closes the editor.
- Added blocks, a power system's **Levels** and an item's **Build tree** are sections of the page instead of boxes. **+ Block** is in the note's header.
- Characters have Bio and Skills sections, a chapter slider with stats, relations and inventory in the column, and Relations, Inventory and Ledger tabs. Blank stats are hidden unless the template shows them.
- Headings above a list of small fields no longer draw a double line.

## The column

- **Teaching**: what an item teaches as a tree, and on an ability what teaches it, stepping through several sources.
- **Race lineage** and the **values of a ranked taxonomy** as trees (these replace the horizontal strip of ranks).
- Plots and volumes link the volume, its main plot and its subplots to each other.
- Stepping through the column changes only the page: the column stays put and keeps your place. It has arrows instead of a scrollbar, and long titles end with ….

## Planning and chapters

- **Change number** on a chapter's plan renumbers the chapter, its plan, its ledger entries and every link together. Swap two chapters, or make room and move the others along.
- **Archive** a chapter with its plan, restore it under any free number, or delete it from the archive.
- Every plan has a chapter note, made automatically, and the two have one title: change it in either and the other follows, with the file name.
- A live and an archived chapter can't have the same number and title.
- Volumes show a **Main plot** section and a **Subplots** section, editable in place, without explanatory text and with more space between plots.
- Planned chapters without text no longer count as the latest chapter.

## Taxonomies and power levels

- One set of levels can belong to several power systems. Link, change or unlink a taxonomy from the power system's page; other systems keep theirs.
- Delete a whole taxonomy from its page. Required taxonomies, and ones a stat template uses, are protected; single values can always be deleted.

## AI assistant

- It can propose taxonomies: create one with its values, add values, link or unlink power systems, or remove one. Every change still goes through the review panel.
- With the AI tab in both drawers, both show the same conversation with bubbles, cards and links, at the same size. Clicking one moves the terminal there.
- **Back to the conversation** goes to the drawer holding it, and both tabs carry on after a restart.

## Drawers, writer and keyboard

- Any side-drawer tab can open on the left, beside the writer.
- Alt+Left / Alt+Right go back and forward in the page, the drawer or the left drawer, whichever you used last.
- Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V work on selected blocks.
- Double-click edits a block or ledger entry, and Escape twice discards a new item.

## Fixes

- Picking a link into a property no longer crashes the drawer, and a page that crashes no longer takes the app with it.
- Links that include a folder follow a note that moves to another folder.
- The drawer no longer jumps to the top when you open a related note.
- Left-drawer tabs no longer get mixed up after following a link and reopening the same page.

## Good to know

- A plan's empty chapter note is in `Chapters/`, so Templater scripts that look for the newest chapter will find it.
- After updating, press **New** in the AI tab so Claude Code loads the new list of what it can propose.
- The Windows installer isn't signed and the macOS app isn't notarized; see the README for the first start.
